title: Connect your platform
body:
# Connect your platform

This guide takes another system from nothing to a working integration: calling the API,
saving documents, and chatting with an agent. Every call here was run against a real
install. Replace `{{BASE_URL}}` with the address of the workspace and keep keys in your
own secret store.

## 1. What you need from the workspace owner

| You want to | Ask for | It looks like | It works on |
|---|---|---|---|
| Call the platform as a program: upload files, fill a knowledge base, manage agents, chat | a **service-account key** | `ak_<id>.sk_<secret>` | `/api/v1/...` |
| Let another product talk to **one** published agent | an **agent key** | `ara_<id><secret>` | `/v1/agents/<slug>/...` |

The two are not interchangeable. An agent key on `/api/v1` is refused with `403`, and a
service-account key is not read on `/v1`.

A workspace administrator creates a service account and its key on **Settings → Service
accounts**, choosing what the account will do. The key is shown once. An agent key is
created on the agent's **Expose** tab.

What a service account creates (files, documents, conversations) belongs to that account,
not to a person.

## 2. Check that the key works

```bash
export CURA_KEY='ak_....sk_....'
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/agents -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY"
```

`200` with `{"items": [...]}` means the key is valid and may read agents. `401` means the
key is wrong, expired or revoked. `403` names the permission the key lacks.

## 3. Send files and build a knowledge base

Upload a file. The form field names are `upload` and, optionally, `mime_type`:

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/files:upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" \
  -F "upload=@handbook.md" -F "mime_type=text/markdown"
```

The reply has the file's `id` and, once it is read, a `documentId` in the document
library. `GET /api/v1/files:limits` gives the types and the size this workspace accepts.

Create a knowledge base (a collection) and add the file to it:

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/knowledge/collections \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug":"handbook","name":"Handbook"}'

curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/knowledge/collections/$COLLECTION_ID/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"fileIds":["'$FILE_ID'"]}'
```

The workspace needs an embedding model before a collection can be created; without one
the reply is `409` and says so. Search it:

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/knowledge/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"when does the visitor desk open","collectionIds":["'$COLLECTION_ID'"],"topK":5}'
```

More ways to add documents (a web address, a whole site from its sitemap, pasted text) are
in [Documents and knowledge bases](?note=documents-and-knowledge).

## 4. Chat with an agent

With a service-account key, on `/api/v1`:

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/conversations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"agentId":"'$AGENT_ID'"}'

curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/conversations/$CONVERSATION_ID/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Summarise the handbook.","fileIds":["'$FILE_ID'"]}'
```

The second call answers `202` with `{message, run}`. Follow the run at
`GET /api/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/events` (server-sent events) and read the finished reply from
`GET /api/v1/conversations/$CONVERSATION_ID`.

With an agent key, on `/v1`, one call waits for the reply:

```bash
export AGENT_KEY='ara_....'
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}:run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"text":"What are your opening hours?"}'
```

The reply has `output` (the text), `content` (the parts, citations among them), `usage`
and `runId`. For a conversation with several turns, attaching and mentioning documents,
streaming, and structured answers, see [Chat from your application](?note=chat).

## 5. Work that takes a long time

Send `"wait": false` to get `202` at once with `runId` and `eventsUrl`. Add
`"callbackUrl"` to be told when the run ends. The callback carries only
`{"runId", "status"}` and is signed; fetch the reply with
`GET /v1/agents/<slug>/runs/$RUN_ID`. Details and the signature check are in
[Without the console](?note=without-the-console) and [Webhooks](?note=webhooks).

A run that needs a person's approval stops with status `waiting_approval` until someone
decides it.

## 6. Put the chat on your own site

The workspace's **Channels** screen creates a widget and gives a script tag to paste into
your page. A widget is either open to anyone who visits, with limits on what a visitor
can send, or for people your site has signed in, for whom your server signs a short-lived
token. See [Embed the chat](?note=embed), and [PHP and CMS sites](?note=php-cms) for WordPress,
Drupal, Joomla and plain PHP.

## 7. Let the agent call your platform

An agent reaches your system through tools. Import your OpenAPI document on the **Tools**
screen to turn its operations into tools, keep your credentials in a named connection, or
expose an MCP server. To be told about events, register a webhook
(`POST /api/v1/webhooks`). The other direction, calling an agent as a tool from your own
agent, is the MCP endpoint `/v1/mcp` and A2A ([a2a.md](?note=a2a)).

## 8. Rules every call follows

- **Errors** are `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. Switch on `code`.
- **Idempotency**: send `Idempotency-Key` on a `POST` that starts work. A retry with the
  same key and body returns the same result.
- **Rate limits**: `429` carries `Retry-After`. Agent keys have a per-minute rate and a
  monthly quota set where the key was made.
- **Lists** are paged: `{items, nextCursor, hasMore}`, with `limit` and `cursor`.
- **Field names** are camelCase. An unknown field in a request body is refused with `422`.
  Ignore fields in a reply that you do not know.
- **Keys**: the part before `.sk_` is safe to log; the secret is not. Rotating a key gives
  a new secret and stops the old one at once. Revoking stops the key.

What does not yet behave as the contract says is listed in
[Known differences](?note=known-differences).

title: Integrating over the API — getting started
body:
# Integrating over the API — getting started

For a walk-through from first key to a working chat, start with
[Connect your platform](?note=connect-your-platform).

This is the developer guide for calling the platform from another system. There are two
surfaces, each with its own credential:

| Surface | Base path | Credential | Use it to |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Management API** | `/api/v1` | a **service-account key + secret** (`ak_<prefix>.sk_<secret>`) | manage tenants, agents, knowledge, usage — everything the web app does |
| **Agent API** | `/v1` | an **agent key** (`ara_<prefix><secret>`) | call a published agent (chat, MCP, A2A) from another product |

Pick the management API for machine-to-machine automation that acts as a service account; pick
the agent API to expose one published agent to an external caller or tool. The machine-readable
contracts are the root `openapi.json` (management) and
`/v1/openapi.json` (agent API). Full conventions:
[api-conventions.md](?note=../05-contracts/api-conventions).

## 1. Service-account integration (`/api/v1`)

### Create a service account and a key + secret

A tenant admin creates a service account on **Settings → Service accounts**, which also
gives it a role and a key in one step. Over the API it is three calls: create the account
(`POST /api/v1/service-accounts`), give it a role (`POST /api/v1/role-assignments` with
`principalType: "service_account"`), then mint a key:

```bash
curl -s https://runtime.example/api/v1/api-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin session or key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"ci-bot","serviceAccountId":"<sa-id>","scopes":["agents:read","chat:use"]}'
```

The response returns the credential **once**:

```json
{ "id": "...", "name": "ci-bot", "prefix": "ab12cd34ef56", "keyFormat": "split",
  "scopes": ["agents:read","chat:use"], "key": "ak_ab12cd34ef56.sk_<secret>" }
```

Store `key` securely — later reads return everything **except** the secret. The key id
(`ak_<prefix>`) is safe to log; the `sk_` secret is not.

The calls, all for a workspace administrator:

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/service-accounts:capabilities` | What an account can be made for, with the role and permissions for each |
| `POST /api/v1/service-accounts` | Create an account |
| `PATCH /api/v1/service-accounts/{service_account_id}` | Describe it, or disable it (`status: "disabled"`) |
| `DELETE /api/v1/service-accounts/{service_account_id}` | Delete it. What it created stays |
| `POST /api/v1/api-keys` | Mint a key for it (`serviceAccountId`, `scopes`, `expiresInDays`) |
| `GET /api/v1/api-keys?serviceAccountId=` | Its keys, without their secrets |
| `POST /api/v1/api-keys/{api_key_id}:rotate` | A new secret for a key; the old one stops at once |
| `DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/{api_key_id}` | Revoke a key |

### Authenticate

Send the whole credential as a bearer token:

```bash
curl -s https://runtime.example/api/v1/agents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ak_ab12cd34ef56.sk_<secret>"
```

The caller resolves to a **service-account principal** in the key's tenant. Its permissions are
the service account's role grants **intersected with the key's `scopes`** — a key can only ever
be a subset of what its service account may do. A request for anything outside that set is
`403 forbidden`.

### Rotate and revoke

- **Rotate** issues a new secret, keeps the key id, and invalidates the old secret immediately:
  the response carries the new `key` once. Rotate on a schedule and on suspected exposure.
- **Revoke** disables the key; later calls are `401 unauthenticated`.

(Legacy single-token `ark_...` keys created before the split format keep working.)

## 2. Agent integration (`/v1`)

See [README.md](?note=readme) for the full REST / MCP / A2A walkthrough. In short: create an agent
key on the agent's **Expose** tab, then either hold a conversation, or use the **one-shot run**
for a single stateless call:

```bash
# One-shot: creates an ephemeral conversation, runs once, returns the reply + usage.
curl -s https://runtime.example/v1/agents/<slug>:run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ara_<prefix><secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"text":"...","stream":false}'
```

The reply includes `usage` with `tokensIn`, `tokensOut` and `costMicros`. A retry with the same
`Idempotency-Key` returns the same run. For a multi-turn conversation, create one and post
messages instead:

```bash
curl -s https://runtime.example/v1/agents/<slug>/conversations/$CONVERSATION_ID/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ara_<prefix><secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"text":"...","stream":true}'
```

## 3. The contract every caller relies on

These apply to both surfaces (details in [api-conventions.md](?note=../05-contracts/api-conventions)):

- **Errors** are RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code`
  field clients switch on (`unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `validation_failed`,
  `rate_limited`, `quota_exceeded`, `conflict`, …). See the
  [error code table](?note=../05-contracts/api-conventions#5-errors-rfc-9457-problem-details).
- **Idempotency**: every `POST` that starts work accepts `Idempotency-Key`; a replay with the
  same key and body returns the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key
  with a different body is `409 idempotency_key_reused`.
- **Pagination** is cursor-based: `limit` (1–200) and `cursor`, with a
  `{ items, nextCursor, hasMore }` envelope.
- **Rate limits**: every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and
  `RateLimit-Reset`. A `429 rate_limited` includes `Retry-After`; a `429 quota_exceeded` means a
  block-action quota is exhausted, with `{ quotaId, metric, period, limit, used, resetsAt }`.
  Back off and retry after the stated window.
- **Versioning**: the base path is versioned (`/api/v1`, `/v1`). Additive changes (new fields,
  new endpoints, new *open* enum values) happen in place — **clients must ignore unknown response
  fields**. A breaking change ships under a new major path; deprecations are announced before
  removal.
- **Usage & cost**: run responses carry a usage summary (tokens in/out, model/tool calls and
  `costMicros`); per-tenant and per-key usage is available from the usage API for chargeback.

## 4. Checklist

1. Create a service account (management) or expose an agent (agent API).
2. Mint a key; capture the secret shown once.
3. Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; handle `401`/`403` and refresh on rotation.
4. Send `Idempotency-Key` on writes; honour `RateLimit-*` and `429 Retry-After`.
5. Ignore unknown response fields; switch on the error `code`, never the HTTP phrase.

title: Documents and knowledge bases
body:
# Documents and knowledge bases

All of these use a service-account key on `/api/v1`. Replace `{{BASE_URL}}`.

## Upload a file

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/files:upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" \
  -F "upload=@policy.pdf" -F "mime_type=application/pdf"
```

Form fields: `upload` (the file), `mime_type`, `expires_after_seconds`,
`replaces_file_id`. These four are snake_case; JSON bodies are camelCase. The reply:
`id`, `name`, `mimeType`, `sizeBytes`, `status`, and `documentId` once the file has been
read into the library. `415` means the type is not accepted and `413` that it is too
large; `GET /api/v1/files:limits` says what is.

Needs `chat:use`.

## The document library

Every readable upload becomes a library document: its text split into passages, each
with an anchor such as `p1-s0`.

| Call | What it gives |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/library-documents` (form field `upload`) | upload straight into the library |
| `GET /api/v1/library-documents` | the documents you can see |
| `GET /api/v1/library-documents/{id}` | one document, with its outline |
| `GET /api/v1/library-documents/{id}/passages?pageFrom=&pageTo=` | its text, passage by passage |
| `GET /api/v1/library-documents/{id}/diff?otherDocumentId=` | what changed between two documents |
| `DELETE /api/v1/library-documents/{id}` | remove it |

## Save documents to a knowledge base

A knowledge base is a collection. An agent that lists the collection answers from it and
cites it. The workspace needs an embedding model first.

**Create a collection** (`knowledge:manage`):

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/knowledge/collections \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug":"policies","name":"Policies","visibility":"tenant"}'
```

**Add files you uploaded.** Up to 100 at a time; each must be ready and uploaded by the
same account:

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/knowledge/collections/$COLLECTION_ID/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"fileIds":["'$FILE_ID'"]}'
```

**Add one document another way**, with
`POST /api/v1/knowledge/collections/$COLLECTION_ID/members`:

| `kind` | Send | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| `library` | `libraryDocumentId` | a document already in the library |
| `url` | `url`, `title` (optional) | the page at that address |
| `text` | `text`, `title`, `externalId` (optional) | text you send |

The reply says `indexed` or `unchanged`. Sending the same text again changes nothing;
`"force": true` indexes it again.

**Keep a whole site in step.** Add a web source that starts at the site's sitemap and
let it sync on a schedule. The host must be on the workspace's web-access list.

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/knowledge/collections/$COLLECTION_ID/sources \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Website","kind":"web","syncSchedule":"0 3 * * *",
       "config":{"start_urls":["https://example.com/sitemap.xml"],"allowed_domains":["example.com"],"max_pages":200,"max_depth":0}}'

curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/knowledge/sources/$SOURCE_ID:sync \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"mode":"incremental"}'
```

A start address may be a page, a sitemap, a sitemap index or a feed. Each page becomes one
document under its own title and address, so an answer that cites it links to the page.
`max_depth` 1 also reads what those pages link to on the same site, such as PDFs. The
site's robots.txt is always followed, an unchanged page is not read again, and a page
that has left the sitemap is removed.

The sync answers `202` with a `jobId`. `GET /api/v1/knowledge/jobs/$JOB_ID` gives its
`status` and `stats` (`added`, `updated`, `unchanged`, `deleted`, `failed`);
`GET /api/v1/knowledge/collections/$COLLECTION_ID/jobs` lists a collection's jobs, and
`POST /api/v1/knowledge/jobs/$JOB_ID:cancel` stops one.
`GET /api/v1/knowledge/collections/$COLLECTION_ID` gives the collection and its counts.

**Search** (`knowledge:read`):

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/knowledge/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"notice period","collectionIds":["'$COLLECTION_ID'"],"topK":5}'
```

Each hit has `title`, `uri`, `snippet`, `score`, `pageFrom`, `pageTo`, `documentId` and
`collectionId`.

title: Chat from your application
body:
# Chat from your application

Two ways in. A **service-account key** uses `/api/v1/conversations` and can do everything
a signed-in person can. An **agent key** uses `/v1/agents/<slug>/...` and reaches one
published agent. Replace `{{BASE_URL}}` and `{{AGENT_SLUG}}`.

## A conversation with an agent key

```bash
curl -s -X POST {{BASE_URL}}/v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}/conversations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_KEY"

curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}/conversations/$CONVERSATION_ID/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"text":"What is our notice period?"}'
```

The reply, once the agent has finished:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `output` | the answer as text |
| `content` | the answer as parts: text, files, images, citations, follow-ups |
| `status`, `finishReason` | how the turn ended |
| `usage` | `tokensIn`, `tokensOut`, `toolCalls`, `costMicros`, `elapsedMs` |
| `runId`, `conversationId` | to fetch the trace or send the next message |

Send the next message to the same conversation to continue it. For one question with no
history, `POST /v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}:run` with the same body does both steps.

Body fields: `text`, `fileIds`, `attachmentIds`, `collectionIds`, `taskTemplate`, `items`,
`responseFormat`, `suggestFollowups`, `stream`, `wait`, `callbackUrl`.

## Attach documents

Upload first, then name the file on the message.

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}/files \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_KEY" -F "upload=@contract.pdf"

curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}/conversations/$CONVERSATION_ID/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"What is the notice period in this contract?","fileIds":["'$FILE_ID'"]}'
```

- `fileIds` and `attachmentIds` both take file ids and are treated alike.
- A file can be used when the caller uploaded it, when it is in a collection the caller
  can read, or when it was given to the agent.
- `collectionIds` points the turn at whole knowledge bases.
- With a service-account key the same fields go on
  `POST /api/v1/conversations/$CONVERSATION_ID/messages`, and files are uploaded with
  `POST /api/v1/files:upload`.

## Mention documents

In the product, type `@` in the message box, or press **Documents**, and pick one or more
documents from the library. They appear as chips on the message.

Over the API a mention is the same thing as an attachment: put the file id of each
document in `fileIds`. A library document's file id is the `fileId` field of
`GET /api/v1/library-documents`.

## Read citations

A cited answer has `citation_ref` parts in `content`:

```json
{"type": "citation_ref", "index": 1,
 "citation": {"index": 1, "sourceKind": "knowledge", "title": "Handbook",
              "uri": "https://example.com/handbook", "snippet": "The desk opens at 08:30.",
              "pageFrom": 1, "pageTo": 1, "documentId": "...", "collectionId": "..."}}
```

`sourceKind` is `knowledge` for a knowledge base and `document` for an attached file; a
`document` citation has `anchor`, `page` and `fileId`. Read citations from `content` on
the reply. The event stream does not carry all of them.

## Stream, or do not wait

- `"stream": true` returns `text/event-stream`: the run's events (`message.delta` with
  `text`, `tool_call.*`, `subagent.*`, `run.completed`), then a final `done` event with
  `output` and `status`. The events are sent once the turn has finished.
- `"wait": false` returns `202` with `runId` and `eventsUrl` at once. Follow
  `GET /v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}/runs/$RUN_ID/events`, or give a `callbackUrl`.
- With a service-account key, `GET /api/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/events` streams a run as it
  happens. Resume with `Last-Event-ID`.

## A structured answer

Send a JSON Schema as `responseFormat`. The answer is JSON that matches it, or the turn
fails saying it could not produce one.

```bash
curl -s {{BASE_URL}}/v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}:run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Extract the parties.","fileIds":["'$FILE_ID'"],
       "responseFormat":{"type":"object","properties":{"parties":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["parties"]}}'
```

## The same from Python and JavaScript

```python
import httpx

api = httpx.Client(base_url="{{BASE_URL}}", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {AGENT_KEY}"}, timeout=300)
reply = api.post("/v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}:run", json={"text": "What are your opening hours?"}).json()
print(reply["output"])
for part in reply["content"]:
    if part["type"] == "citation_ref":
        print(part["citation"]["title"], part["citation"]["uri"])
```

```javascript
const reply = await fetch("{{BASE_URL}}/v1/agents/{{AGENT_SLUG}}:run", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${AGENT_KEY}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ text: "What are your opening hours?" }),
}).then((response) => response.json());
console.log(reply.output);
```

## Other ways to reach an agent

| Way | Where |
|---|---|
| MCP | `POST /v1/mcp` or `/v1/agents/<slug>/mcp`, agent key |
| A2A | `/v1/agents/<slug>/a2a` and the agent card; see [a2a.md](?note=a2a) |
| OpenAI-compatible | `POST /api/v1/openai/chat/completions`, service-account key, `model` is the agent's slug; `GET /api/v1/openai/models` lists the agents as models |
| Research | `POST /v1/research/runs` starts a longer, multi-step research run with an agent key; `GET /v1/research/runs/{run_id}` and `/v1/research/runs/{run_id}/events` follow it |

title: Calling an agent from another product
body:
# Calling an agent from another product

New to the API? Start with the [getting-started guide](?note=getting-started), which also covers
service-account integration on `/api/v1`.

A published agent has its own keys. Create one on the agent's Expose tab. The secret is shown once. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer ara_...`.

The contract is `GET /v1/openapi.json`. A copy generated from those routes is openapi.json.

Replace `https://runtime.example` and `ara_...` with the origin that serves `/v1` and a real key.

## REST

Create a conversation, then send a message. `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry return the same run.

```bash
curl -s https://runtime.example/v1/agents/assistant/conversations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ara_<prefix><secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

```bash
curl -s https://runtime.example/v1/agents/assistant/conversations/$CONVERSATION_ID/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ara_<prefix><secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: retry-1" \
  -d '{"text":"What is 2 + 2?"}'
```

Stream the same call with `"stream": true`. The response is `text/event-stream` with the run's events (`message.delta` carries the text) and a final `done` event. The events are sent once the turn has finished.

```javascript
const base = "https://runtime.example/v1/agents/assistant";
const headers = {
  Authorization: "Bearer ara_<prefix><secret>",
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
};
const created = await fetch(`${base}/conversations`, { method: "POST", headers });
const conversation = await created.json();
const reply = await fetch(`${base}/conversations/${conversation.id}/messages`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { ...headers, "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID() },
  body: JSON.stringify({ text: "What is 2 + 2?" }),
});
console.log(await reply.json());
```

Attach a file first, then pass its id:

```bash
curl -s https://runtime.example/v1/agents/assistant/files \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ara_<prefix><secret>" \
  -F "upload=@notes.txt" \
  -F "mime_type=text/plain"
```

The trace for that run, and only that run, is `GET /v1/agents/assistant/runs/$RUN_ID`. Events are `GET /v1/agents/assistant/runs/$RUN_ID/events`.

A finished reply includes `content`, the same parts the product stores (text, files, images, citations, follow-ups). `reasoning.delta` is omitted unless you pass `includeReasoning=true` and the agent has `showReasoning` on. Optional `responseFormat` is a JSON Schema for that turn. `suggestFollowups` asks for a `followups` part.

Samples: [document review and a chart](?note=samples). Webhooks: [signatures](?note=webhooks).

## MCP

Streamable HTTP. One tool is listed per published agent the key may call. A workspace-scoped key lists every published agent in the tenant.

Cursor (`.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "assistant": {
      "url": "https://runtime.example/v1/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ara_<prefix><secret>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "assistant": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://runtime.example/v1/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ara_<prefix><secret>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

A generic client posts JSON-RPC to the same URL:

```bash
curl -s https://runtime.example/v1/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ara_<prefix><secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

`tools/call` takes `message`. A write uses `write.tool` and `write.arguments`. If the policy gate holds the write, the tool result text is `Approval required` and `structuredContent.status` is `approval_required`.

## Errors, rate limits and versioning

The `/v1` surface follows the platform [API conventions](?note=../05-contracts/api-conventions):

- **Errors** are RFC 9457 Problem Details with a stable `code` (switch on `code`, not the HTTP
  phrase): `401 unauthenticated` (missing/invalid/expired key), `404 not_found` (another key's
  run, or an unpublished agent — existence is never revealed), `409 idempotency_key_reused`,
  `429 rate_limited`, `429 quota_exceeded`. See the
  [code table](?note=../05-contracts/api-conventions#5-errors-rfc-9457-problem-details).
- **Rate limits & quota** are per key. Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`,
  `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`; a `429 rate_limited` carries `Retry-After`. Each
  key has a requests-per-minute limit (`rateLimitRpm`) and a monthly quota (`monthlyQuota`,
  `0` = unlimited).
- **Idempotency**: message send accepts `Idempotency-Key`; the same key and body return the
  stored reply without starting a second run; a different body is `idempotency_key_reused`.
- **Versioning**: additive changes happen in `/v1` — ignore unknown response fields. A breaking
  change ships under a new major path. Responses carry `API-Version: 1`. `GET /v1` returns
  `{"version": "1"}`.
- **Streams**: `POST` with `"stream": true`, and `GET /v1/agents/{slug}/runs/{runId}/events`,
  are `text/event-stream`. Resume with `Last-Event-ID` (a sequence or `{runId}:{seq}`). The
  server replays from the shared run-event stream, sends `: ping` heartbeats while the run
  is still working, and closes after the tail. `Accept: application/json` on the events
  route returns one cursor page (`items`, `nextCursor`, `hasMore`).

## Rotating and revoking a key

Rotate a key from the Expose tab (or `POST /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/api-keys/{keyId}:rotate`):
the new secret is shown once and the old one stops working immediately. Revoke deletes it;
later calls are `401`. Keys are stored as a SHA-256 hash and never returned after creation.

## A2A

See [a2a.md](?note=a2a).

title: Samples
Using an agent without the console
body:
# Using an agent without the console

People who approve work, and systems that start work, do not need an account in the web console.

## Call an agent

`POST /v1/agents/{slug}:run` with `Authorization: Bearer <agent key>`. Send `wait: false` and `callbackUrl` to be told when the run ends, by a signed POST (`X-Signature`, the tenant run-callback secret), instead of holding the connection. The POST carries `{runId, status}`; fetch the reply with `GET /v1/agents/{slug}/runs/{runId}`. Upload a file first with `POST /v1/agents/{slug}/files`. The same key opens MCP (`POST /v1/agents/{slug}/mcp`) and A2A (`POST /v1/a2a`).

Keys are created in the console, or by someone who already has `agents:edit`, and are shown once.

## Decide an approval from a link or a card

When a tool needs a person, and the tenant has a Slack or Teams binding (or the approver has linked their account), the approver gets a card with Approve, Reject and Review. The review link is `{AR_PUBLIC_URL}/review/{token}`. It shows that one request, rendered from the tool's JSON Schema, and accepts an edit. Approving with edited values keeps the original and the edited arguments.

Mail goes to the approvers named by the policy (the requester, a list of users, a group, or the agent owner). `AR_APPROVAL_NOTIFY_EMAIL` adds one more address. It is empty unless an install sets it.

If the install signs people in with OIDC (`AR_AUTH_MODE=oidc`), the link still names the item and the approver must sign in as that person. Otherwise the signed link is the credential. A guest session cannot decide.

## Receive events

`POST /api/v1/webhooks` with `webhooks:manage` stores a subscription on `outbound_webhooks`. The response includes `secret` once. Each delivery is a camelCase JSON body signed with `X-AR-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, over `timestamp + "." + body`, plus `X-AR-Event-Id` and `X-AR-Topic`. Retries follow the backoff in `ar_domain.events.sign`. `POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{deliveryId}:redeliver` sends one again.

Public topics include `approval.requested`, `approval.decided`, `run.completed`, `run.failed`, `document.ingested` and `extraction.completed`. Payloads carry ids and status, not document text.

A customer Slack workspace, Teams tenant or mail server was not used to prove the live send. The card is built and, when the binding stores a bot token or an incoming webhook URL, posted by the channels service. The signature check is proven against a local receiver.

title: Webhooks
Embed the chat
body:
# Embed the chat

A workspace administrator creates a widget on the **Channels** screen: its name, the
agent it talks to, who can chat, and the exact origins of the pages allowed to show it.
Widgets are off in a new workspace; the same screen turns them on ("Website and portal
chat"), which needs the right to manage the workspace. A saved widget is changed, turned
off or deleted from its row, and **Install code** shows its script tag again:

```html
<script src="{{BASE_URL}}/widget.js" data-integration="<widget id>" defer></script>
```

The script adds a button that opens the chat in a frame. `data-label` sets the button's
text. For WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and plain PHP, see [PHP and CMS sites](?note=php-cms).

The agent must be one the people behind the widget may use: on the agent's page set
**Who can use it** to "Everyone in the workspace". The Channels screen says when the
chosen agent is not.

**Sources.** An answer carries the numbers of the passages it cites, and a **Sources**
button under it opens the list when the visitor asks: one line per page, with the numbers
the answer gave it; a web page is a link that opens in a new tab, and any other source is
named only. A widget whose **Let visitors see the sources an answer cites** is off
(`showSources: false`) receives no source at all: the API takes them out of the
conversation before the widget reads it.

A widget is one of two kinds.

## Anyone who visits the site

Nobody signs in and the page needs nothing but the script tag. Each visitor gets a chat of
their own that nobody else can open, and cannot attach files.

Three things must be true before a visitor can chat:

1. The widget's **Who can chat** is "Anyone who visits the site".
2. It names the **account visitors act as**: an active user of the workspace. Visitors can
   do only what that account can, so give it nothing but the right to chat and to read
   what the agent answers from.
3. The agent is **opened to visitors**: on the agent's Expose tab, "Let people who have
   not signed in chat with this agent", then publish. In a definition file this is
   `channels.public: true`. A widget cannot open an agent whose owner has not.

### What protects a public chat

Anyone can reach a public chat, including a script. These bound what it can use:

| Setting on the widget | Default | What it bounds |
|---|---|---|
| Allowed origins | none | The pages that may show the chat. A browser refuses any other page. |
| Messages in one chat (`maxMessages`) | 30 | How much one visitor's session can send. Starting a new conversation does not reset it. |
| Characters in one message (`maxMessageChars`) | 2000 | The size, and so the cost, of one message. |
| New chats a minute, in all (`sessionsPerMinute`) | 60 | The whole widget, whoever is asking. |
| New chats a minute, one visitor (`sessionsPerClientPerMinute`) | 10 | One address. |
| Minutes a chat stays open (`sessionSeconds`) | 30 | How long a session lasts. |
| What visitors are told first (`notice`) | empty | Shown with a Start chat button before anything is sent. |

And outside the widget:

- **The agent's budget** caps the steps, tokens and cost of each answer.
- **A quota on the account visitors act as** (Quotas screen) is the ceiling for the whole
  month, whatever the traffic.
- **What the agent can reach.** A visitor can ask it anything. Give a public agent only
  knowledge that is public and tools that are safe for anyone to trigger.
- **Turning it off.** Disabling the widget, or clearing the agent's "opened to visitors",
  stops new chats at once.

A limit that is reached answers `429` with words the visitor can read.

**Behind a proxy.** One visitor is told from another by address. The web app and any
ingress in front of the API must be named in `AR_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, or every visitor
looks like the proxy and shares one allowance. A caller that is not a trusted proxy is
counted as itself, whatever `X-Forwarded-For` it sends.

## People your site has signed in

Each person must be a user of the workspace. Your server signs a short-lived token (ten
minutes at most) and your page hands it over when the widget asks:

```javascript
window.addEventListener("ar-widget:token-request", async (event) => {
  const { token } = await fetch("/my-backend/widget-token").then((r) => r.json());
  event.detail.respond(token);
});
```

The token is a JWT signed with the widget's secret (HS256) or your own key (RS256, with
a registered JWKS address). Claims: `sub` (the person's email), `name`, `exp`, and `aud`
set to `ar-widget:<widget id>`. The secret stays on your server.

A person in the widget reaches only the conversation started in that session and only
the agents the widget lists.

## The calls the widget makes

You do not call these yourself; they are listed so a firewall or a reviewer knows them.
All are under `{{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/widget`.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/widget/integrations/{integration_id}` | The widget's name, allowed origins, kind and notice. Public. |
| `POST /api/v1/widget/sessions` | Starts a session: with a token for a signed-in person, with none for a public widget. Sets a cookie scoped to the widget's own path. |
| `GET /api/v1/widget/session` | The agents this session may talk to. |
| `POST /api/v1/widget/conversations` | Starts the session's conversation. |
| `POST /api/v1/widget/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages` | Sends a message. |
| `GET /api/v1/widget/runs/{run_id}/events` | The reply as it is written. |

title: PHP and CMS sites
body:
# PHP and CMS sites

How to put the chat on a site built with a PHP content system. The files named here are
in the repository under `integrations/php/`.

First create the widget on the workspace's **Channels** screen and add your site's origin
(for example `https://www.example.com`, with no path) to its allowed origins. Note the
widget id from the script tag it gives.

## A widget open to anyone

The script tag is all a page needs. Where it goes:

| System | Where to put the script tag |
|---|---|
| WordPress | Install the plugin below; or add the tag to the theme's footer; or a Custom HTML block on one page |
| Drupal | A custom block with full HTML, placed in the footer region; or the theme's `html.html.twig` before `</body>` |
| Joomla | A Custom module with the editor set to none, in a footer position; or the template's `index.php` before `</body>` |
| Any PHP page | Print it before `</body>` |

```php
<script src="{{BASE_URL}}/widget.js" data-integration="<?= htmlspecialchars($widgetId) ?>" defer></script>
```

A site that sends a `Content-Security-Policy` header must allow `{{BASE_URL}}` in
`script-src` and `frame-src`.

## A widget for people signed in to your site

The page also needs a token for the person, signed on your server with the widget's
signing secret. The person's email must belong to a user of the workspace.

`integrations/php/widget-token.php` has one function, with no dependencies:

```php
require __DIR__ . '/widget-token.php';

// An endpoint on your site that only a signed-in person can reach.
header('Content-Type: application/json');
header('Cache-Control: no-store');
echo json_encode(['token' => cura_widget_token(
    getenv('CURA_WIDGET_ID'),
    getenv('CURA_WIDGET_SECRET'),   // never sent to the browser
    $currentUser->email,
    $currentUser->name
)]);
```

And on the page, after the script tag:

```html
<script>
window.addEventListener("ar-widget:token-request", async (event) => {
  const reply = await fetch("/chat-token.php", { credentials: "same-origin" });
  event.detail.respond((await reply.json()).token);
});
</script>
```

The token is good for five minutes by default and ten at most. The widget asks again when
it needs a new one.

## WordPress

`integrations/php/wordpress/cura-works-chat/` is a plugin. Copy the folder into
`wp-content/plugins/`, activate **Cura Works Chat**, and open **Settings → Cura Works
Chat**:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Workspace address | `{{BASE_URL}}` |
| Widget id | from the script tag |
| Where it shows | every page, or only where the `[cura_chat]` shortcode is placed |
| Who can chat | tick for a widget set to "People your portal has signed in" |
| Host signing secret | the widget's secret, for signed-in chat only. It is stored on your server and never printed back |

For signed-in chat the plugin adds a token endpoint that only a signed-in WordPress user
can call, and the person's WordPress email must match a user of the workspace.

## Calling the API from PHP

Chat, files and knowledge bases are plain HTTPS calls. From PHP, with a service-account
key kept on the server:

```php
$ch = curl_init('{{BASE_URL}}/api/v1/knowledge/search');
curl_setopt_array($ch, [
    CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
    CURLOPT_POST => true,
    CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => [
        'Authorization: Bearer ' . getenv('CURA_KEY'),
        'Content-Type: application/json',
    ],
    CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => json_encode(['query' => 'opening hours', 'topK' => 5]),
]);
$hits = json_decode(curl_exec($ch), true)['hits'] ?? [];
```

Never put a key in a page, a theme file a browser can read, or JavaScript. See
[Connect your platform](?note=connect-your-platform) for every call.

title: A2A
body:
# A2A

The agent card is served at:

- `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` with `Authorization: Bearer ara_...` (the key selects the agent)
- `GET /v1/agents/{slug}/.well-known/agent-card.json` with the same header

The card's `url` is `POST /v1/agents/{slug}/a2a`. `POST /v1/a2a` uses the key's agent.

Implemented JSON-RPC methods:

| Method | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `message/send`, `tasks/send` | Run the agent and return the task, including an artifact |
| `message/stream`, `tasks/sendSubscribe` | The same task as `text/event-stream` |
| `tasks/get` | The task this key created |
| `tasks/cancel` | Mark the task canceled and POST any saved webhook |
| `tasks/list` | One page of this key's tasks. `pageSize` defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. `pageToken` is the last task id from the previous page. The result has `tasks` and `nextPageToken` |
| `tasks/pushNotificationConfig/set` | Store `url` and optional `token` for one task. The token is returned to this key on get. It is not written to the audit detail |
| `tasks/pushNotificationConfig/get` | The config for this key and task |
| `tasks/pushNotificationConfig/delete` | Remove that config |
| `tasks/pushNotificationConfig/list` | The configs for one task |

`message/send` accepts `configuration.pushNotificationConfig`. When the task is saved or canceled, the server POSTs the task to each saved URL. A failed POST does not fail the task. The card sets `pushNotifications` to true.

A task that is waiting on approval has `status.state` of `input-required` and the text `Approval required`.

Still not implemented, and not claimed:

- `tasks/resubscribe`
- gRPC

Those methods return JSON-RPC error `-32601`. See [OQ-64](?note=../open-questions).

## Calling a remote agent

Bind `control.a2a_call` on the caller. Arguments are `url` (the remote agent card), `message`, and `secret_name`. Store the remote bearer token with `POST /api/v1/secrets` under that name. The tool reads the secret on the server. Do not put the token in the instructions or the tool arguments the model writes.

The URL must pass the public egress check. Loopback is allowed only in `dev`, `ci` and `test`.

title: Known differences
body:
# Known differences

Where the product does not yet do what an older document or the contract says. These
notes describe what it does today.

| What | Today |
|---|---|
| The callback for a run started with `callbackUrl` | Carries `{"runId", "status"}` only. Fetch the reply with `GET /v1/agents/<slug>/runs/$RUN_ID`. |
| Citations on the event stream | `citation.added` is sent for attached documents, not for knowledge bases. Read citations from `content` on the reply. |
| `message.completed` on the event stream | Carries `messageId`, `text` and `answeredModel`, not the content parts. |
| Stream event names | The stream sends the run's events (`message.delta`, …) and a final `done`. There is no `delta` event. |
| `"stream": true` on `/v1` | The events are sent after the turn has finished, not while it runs. |
| `wait` on `POST /api/v1/runs` | Accepted and not used. |
| A citation's `sourceKind` | Can be `document`, with `anchor`, `page` and `fileId`, which the published schema does not list. |
| Rate limits on service-account keys | None of their own; the workspace's limits apply. Agent keys have a per-key rate and monthly quota. |
| "Last used" on a service-account key | Not recorded yet; it shows as never used. |
